title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
description: Twelve cases from 221B Baker Street, told by Dr Watson: a king's blackmailer, a league of red-headed men, a goose with a jewel in its crop, and a speckled band in a locked room.

cover.alt: Holmes in the stalls at St. James's Hall
cover.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The masked king
elements.text: The King of Bohemia, masked, asks Holmes to recover a photograph that could wreck his marriage. Irene Adler sees through Holmes's disguise and escapes with it.

metadata.source_quote: how the best plans of Mr. Sherlock Holmes were beaten by a woman’s wit.

image.alt: The masked King of Bohemia enters Baker Street
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The League is dissolved
elements.text: A pawnbroker is paid to copy the encyclopaedia for a league of red-headed men, until the office is locked. Holmes finds a tunnel being dug to a bank vault.

metadata.source_quote: “It is quite a three pipe problem, and I beg that you won’t speak to me for fifty minutes.”

image.alt: Jabez Wilson at the locked door of the Red-Headed League
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The vanished fiancé
elements.text: A typist's shy fiancé disappears at the church door. He was her stepfather in disguise, protecting his use of her income.

metadata.source_quote: It has long been an axiom of mine that the little things are infinitely the most important.

image.alt: Windibank, caught like a rat in a trap
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Murder by the pool
elements.text: A young man is arrested for killing his father by a lake. Holmes reads the ground and finds an old man with a secret from the Australian goldfields.

metadata.source_quote: There is nothing more deceptive than an obvious fact

image.alt: The Boscombe Pool, where Charles McCarthy was found
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Five pips in an envelope
elements.text: Five orange pips arrive before each death in a family. Holmes is too late to save his client and takes it as a wound to his pride.

metadata.source_quote: I have been beaten four times—three times by men, and once by a woman.

image.alt: Watson: 'Holmes, you are too late'
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The beggar of Threadneedle Street
elements.text: A respectable man vanishes in an opium den. He turns out to be the scarred beggar Hugh Boone, who earns more by begging than by work.

metadata.act: The Man with the Twisted Lip

image.alt: Mrs St. Clair at the opium den in Upper Swandam Lane
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: A goose for Christmas
elements.text: A stolen jewel turns up in a Christmas goose. Holmes traces it back to the thief, and lets him go.

metadata.source_quote: I suppose that I am commuting a felony, but it is just possible that I am saving a soul.

image.alt: James Ryder begs for mercy
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The speckled band
elements.text: Helen Stoner fears she will die like her sister, behind a bolted door. Holmes keeps watch in the dark and meets the swamp adder her stepfather uses.

metadata.source_quote: When a doctor does go wrong he is the first of criminals.

image.alt: 'Good-bye, and be brave': Holmes and Helen Stoner
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: A night's work at Eyford
elements.text: A young engineer hired for a secret job loses his thumb escaping a coining press disguised as a hydraulic machine.

image.alt: Colonel Stark: 'Not a word to a soul'
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The vanishing bride
elements.text: Lord St. Simon's American bride disappears from the wedding breakfast. Her first husband, believed dead, has come back.

image.alt: The wedding of Lord St. Simon
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The broken coronet
elements.text: A banker finds his son holding a damaged national treasure. Holmes, in disguise, clears the son and recovers the missing stones.

image.alt: Holmes confronts Sir George Burnwell
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The governess
elements.text: A governess is paid well to cut her hair and sit in a blue dress. Holmes finds a daughter locked in a remote house.

metadata.source_quote: the lowest and vilest alleys in London do not present a more dreadful record of sin than does the smiling and beautiful countryside.

image.alt: Violet Hunter meets Holmes and Watson at Winchester
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Sherlock Holmes
elements.text: The consulting detective of 221B Baker Street: violinist, master of disguise, reader of trifles, bored to death between cases.

metadata.source_quote: My name is Sherlock Holmes. It is my business to know what other people don’t know.

image.alt: Holmes in the stalls at St. James's Hall
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Dr John Watson
elements.text: Holmes's friend and chronicler, a doctor with a practical mind who asks the questions the reader would ask.

metadata.source_quote: You see, but you do not observe.

image.alt: Watson: 'Holmes, you are too late'
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Irene Adler
elements.text: An opera singer and adventuress who outwits Holmes and keeps the King's photograph as insurance. Forever "the woman".

metadata.source_quote: To Sherlock Holmes she is always the woman.

image.alt: The wedding of Lord St. Simon
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The King of Bohemia
elements.text: A huge, masked royal client who wants his old letters and photograph back before his wedding.

image.alt: The masked King of Bohemia enters Baker Street
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Jabez Wilson
elements.text: A red-headed pawnbroker who copies the encyclopaedia for weeks without asking why.

image.alt: Jabez Wilson at the locked door of the Red-Headed League
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Helen Stoner
elements.text: A frightened young woman whose sister died crying out about a speckled band.

image.alt: 'Good-bye, and be brave': Holmes and Helen Stoner
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: James Ryder
elements.text: The hotel attendant who stole the blue carbuncle and hid it in a goose.

image.alt: James Ryder begs for mercy
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: 221B Baker Street
elements.text: Holmes's rooms: a fire, two armchairs, a sofa, chemical stains and seventeen steps from the hall.

image.alt: Holmes welcomes Miss Mary Sutherland
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: St. James's Hall
elements.text: The concert hall where Holmes spends an afternoon listening to the violinist Sarasate while a bank robbery goes on underground.

image.alt: Holmes in the stalls at St. James's Hall
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Stoke Moran
elements.text: A crumbling manor in Surrey with a bell-pull that rings nothing and a ventilator into the next room.

image.alt: 'Good-bye, and be brave': Holmes and Helen Stoner
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The country lanes
elements.text: Hampshire, Herefordshire, Berkshire: beautiful countryside that Holmes trusts less than London.

image.alt: The Boscombe Pool, where Charles McCarthy was found
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Victorian London
elements.text: Gas-light, hansom cabs, telegrams and fog: a city of strangers where a detective can be hired like a doctor.

image.alt: Watson: 'Holmes, you are too late'
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The method
elements.text: Observation of trifles, then inference to the best explanation, tested against every fact.

metadata.source_quote: You know my method. It is founded upon the observation of trifles.

image.alt: Holmes examines the dead man's boots
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Seeing versus observing
elements.text: Everyone sees the same things; very few notice them. The stories are an education in attention.

metadata.source_quote: You see, but you do not observe.

image.alt: Holmes welcomes Miss Mary Sutherland
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Justice above law
elements.text: Holmes lets the guilty go when prison would make things worse, and answers to his own conscience, not the police.

image.alt: James Ryder begs for mercy
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Strangeness hides in the ordinary
elements.text: Life is stranger than fiction, and the oddest stories begin with dull details.

metadata.source_quote: life is infinitely stranger than anything which the mind of man could invent.

image.alt: Windibank, caught like a rat in a trap
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Logic over sensation
elements.text: Holmes complains that Watson's stories turn lessons in reasoning into adventures.

metadata.source_quote: Crime is common. Logic is rare.

elements.title: Joseph Bell
elements.text: Doyle's teacher at Edinburgh, who diagnosed patients' jobs and travels at a glance; the model for Holmes.

elements.title: The Strand Magazine
elements.text: Where the stories first appeared, monthly, from July 1891, with Sidney Paget's illustrations.

image.alt: Holmes confronts Sir George Burnwell
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Gustave Flaubert
elements.text: Holmes quotes Flaubert's letter to George Sand: the man is nothing, the work is everything.
